newsitem.title: USA: Iowa governor mulls tax cuts for coming year.
newsitem.headline: Iowa governor mulls tax cuts for coming year.

text.p: Iowa Gov. Terry Brandstad is considering broad-based tax cuts for the legislature to consider next year, according to his spokesman.
Eric Woolson, the spokesman, said Wednesday that Branstad is looking at reducing inheritance, property and income taxes, as well as tax simplification and reform.

He said the tax cuts, which he added could be "substantial," were spurred by the fact Iowa ended fiscal 1996 on June 30 with an approximately $600 million balance as measured on a generally accepted accounting principles basis.
Branstad is also reviewing budget recommendations from a special commission that began meeting last summer, according to Woolson.

The so-called Fisher Commission, chaired by Des Moines businessman David Fisher, recommended preparing four-year financial projections and instituting reforms of the Rebuild Iowa Infrastructure Fund, among other things.
